math.title: Two inlets and a drain — rates and fill times
math.context:
Two inlet pipes and one drain serve a tank.

Pipe A alone fills the empty tank in $6$ hours.
Pipe B alone fills the empty tank in $4$ hours.
The drain alone empties a full tank in $12$ hours.

All three run together from empty. Decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: A’s fill rate is strictly greater than $\tfrac{1}{5}$ tank per hour.
The combined net rate of A, B and the drain is exactly $\tfrac{5}{12}$ tank per hour.
Starting from empty with all three open, the tank is full in strictly less than $3$ hours.
If only A and the drain run (B closed), the tank still fills, and the time needed exceeds $8$ hours.
B alone fills more of the tank in $1$ hour than A and the drain together add net in $1$ hour.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

A’s rate is $\dfrac{1}{6}$ tank per hour. Compare with $\dfrac{1}{5}$:

$$
\dfrac{1}{6}<\dfrac{1}{5}
$$

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Net rate:

$$
\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{12}=\dfrac{2}{12}+\dfrac{3}{12}-\dfrac{1}{12}=\dfrac{4}{12}=\dfrac{1}{3}
$$

$$
\dfrac{1}{3}\neq \dfrac{5}{12}
$$

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Time from empty at net rate $\dfrac{1}{3}$ is exactly $3$ hours, not strictly less.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

A with drain only:

$$
\dfrac{1}{6}-\dfrac{1}{12}=\dfrac{1}{12}
$$

Time to fill:

$$
12>8
$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

B’s hourly fill is $\dfrac{1}{4}$. A with drain nets $\dfrac{1}{12}$. Since $\dfrac{1}{4}>\dfrac{1}{12}$, B alone outpaces that net flow.

So the statement is True.
math.solution_overview: Rates: $A=\tfrac{1}{6}$, $B=\tfrac{1}{4}$, drain $=\tfrac{1}{12}$. Net all three $=\tfrac{1}{3}$ (time $3$). A+drain $=\tfrac{1}{12}$ (time $12$).

math.title: Two-route van allocation — linear system
math.context:
Two one-way routes leave a depot. Let $x$ be the number of vans on route North and $y$ the number on route East in a morning wave. The dispatcher records:

$$
x+y=50
$$

$$
3x+2y=130
$$

(The second equation is total driver-hours if North takes $3$ hours and East takes $2$.)

Decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: Exactly $30$ vans take the North route.
The East route carries strictly more vans than the North route.
If each North van costs EUR $40$ in fuel and each East van costs EUR $25$, total fuel for the wave exceeds EUR $1{,}600$.
Replacing the hour equation by $4x+y=140$ (same $x+y=50$) would raise the North count above $30$.
The unique solution $(x,y)$ of the original system lies in the open first quadrant.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

From $x+y=50$ get $y=50-x$. Substitute:

$$
3x+2(50-x)=130
$$

$$
3x+100-2x=130
$$

$$
x=30
$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
y=50-30=20
$$

East has fewer vans than North, not more.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Fuel cost (euros kept in prose):

$$
30\cdot 40+20\cdot 25=1{,}200+500=1{,}700>1{,}600
$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

With $x+y=50$ and $4x+y=140$:

$$
4x+(50-x)=140\Rightarrow 3x=90\Rightarrow x=30
$$

North stays at $30$, not above.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

The unique solution is $(30,20)$ with both coordinates positive.

So the statement is True.
math.solution_overview: Solve $x+y=50$, $3x+2y=130$ to get $(30,20)$. Fuel $1700$. Alternate $4x+y=140$ still gives $x=30$.

math.title: Absolute, radical, and sign inequalities
math.context: Decide whether each inequality claim is true or false. Check every boundary and every compound piece carefully.
statements: The solution set of $|x-3|+|x+1|\le 8$ is exactly $[-3,5]$.
The solution set of $\sqrt{x+2}\ge x$ is exactly $[0,2]$.
Every $x\in(0,1)$ satisfies $\dfrac{x-4}{x+1}<0$.
The inequality $x^{2}-5x+6>0$ holds on $(-\infty,2)\cup(3,+\infty)$.
The system $|x|\le 2$ and $x>0$ has exactly two integer solutions.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Critical points $x=-1$ and $x=3$. Piecewise:

- $x\le -1$: $|x-3|+|x+1|=2-2x\le 8\Rightarrow x\ge -3$, so $[-3,-1]$;
- $-1\le x\le 3$: sum equals $4\le 8$ throughout;
- $x\ge 3$: $2x-2\le 8\Rightarrow x\le 5$.

Union: $[-3,5]$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Domain $x\ge -2$. For $x\in[-2,0)$ the right-hand side is negative while the square root is nonnegative, so the inequality holds on all of $[-2,0)$. On $x\ge 0$ squaring yields $x\in[0,2]$. Full solution $[-2,2]$, not $[0,2]$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\dfrac{x-4}{x+1}<0
$$

on the open interval $(-1,4)$. Every point of $(0,1)$ lies in that set.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

$$
x^{2}-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3)>0
$$

precisely on $(-\infty,2)\cup(3,+\infty)$.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$|x|\le 2$ and $x>0$ give $(0,2]$. The integers there are $1$ and $2$ — exactly two.

So the statement is True.
math.solution_overview: Absolute sum → $[-3,5]$. Radical inequality → $[-2,2]$ (claim too small). Rational sign on $(-1,4)$. Quadratic sign as factored. $|x|\le 2$, $x>0$ → integers $\{1,2\}$.

math.title: Vertical throw — vertex, height checks, landing time
math.context:
A ball is thrown vertically. Height in metres after $t$ seconds is

$$
h(t)=-5t^{2}+20t+2\qquad(t\ge 0)
$$

Decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: The maximum height occurs at $t=2$.
The maximum height is strictly greater than $20$ metres.
The ball is still above $10$ metres at $t=3$.
The positive landing time (when $h=0$) is strictly less than $4$.
Completing the square gives $h(t)=-5(t-2)^{2}+22$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

For $h(t)=-5t^{2}+20t+2$ the vertex is at

$$
t=-\dfrac{b}{2a}=-\dfrac{20}{2\cdot(-5)}=2
$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$
h(2)=-5\cdot 4+20\cdot 2+2=-20+40+2=22>20
$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$
h(3)=-5\cdot 9+20\cdot 3+2=-45+60+2=17>10
$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Solve $-5t^{2}+20t+2=0$, or $5t^{2}-20t-2=0$:

$$
t=\dfrac{20\pm\sqrt{400+40}}{10}=\dfrac{20\pm\sqrt{440}}{10}=2\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{110}}{5}
$$

The positive root is $2+\sqrt{110}/5$. Since $\sqrt{100}=10$ and $\sqrt{121}=11$, one has $\sqrt{110}\approx 10.49$, so

$$
t\approx 2+2.10=4.10\nless 4
$$

So the statement is False.

math.title: Exam-style tasks - 5
math.context: A power model $y=A x^{p}$ is calibrated from data. Decide whether each claim about exponents, scaling, and fitted values is true or false.
statements: A balloon maker has volume proportional to $r^3$. Shrinking radius by $10\%$ is said to reduce volume by $\dfrac{271}{10}\%$.
In a pharmacy trial, concentration follows $C(m)=18m^{-1/2}$. The sample labelled $m=9$ is claimed to have concentration $6$ mg/L.
A cooperative farm follows $H(L)=KL^{2/3}$ for harvest. The forecast says eight times the cultivated area produces $5$ times the crop.
A grain cooperative reaches its promised yield when $40L^{\frac{2}{3}}=360$. The land allocation is stated as $L=27$.
A materials sensor passes data through $g(x)=4x^2$ and then $f(u)=3u^{1/2}$. The composed output for $x=6$ is listed as $24$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Convert the input percentage change to the exact multiplier $\dfrac{9}{10}$ and apply the power exponent:

$$\frac{Y_{\rm new}}{Y_{\rm old}}=(\dfrac{9}{10})^{3}$$

$$\frac{Y_{\rm new}}{Y_{\rm old}}=\dfrac{729}{1000}$$

Translate the output multiplier back to a percentage decrease:

$$\left|\dfrac{729}{1000}-1\right|\cdot100\%=\dfrac{271}{10}\%$$

The direction follows from the multiplier being below $1$:

$$\frac{Y_{\rm new}}{Y_{\rm old}}<1$$

The stem gives $\dfrac{271}{10}\%$, so the decisive comparison is

$$\dfrac{271}{10}\%=\dfrac{271}{10}\%.$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Substitute the recorded input into the stated model:

$$C(9)=\frac{18}{\sqrt{9}}$$

Interpret the rational or negative exponent before doing the final arithmetic:

$$C(9)=\frac{18}{3}$$

Hence the model output is

$$C(9)=6$$

The stem's value is $6$, so the numerical comparison is

$$6=6.$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Form a ratio so the unknown positive coefficient and the original input cancel:

$$\frac{H(8L)}{H(L)}=\frac{K(8L)^{\frac{2}{3}}}{KL^{\frac{2}{3}}}$$

Separate the scale factor from the original power:

$$\frac{H(8L)}{H(L)}=(8)^{\frac{2}{3}}$$

Evaluating that power gives

$$(8)^{\frac{2}{3}}$$

$$\frac{H(8L)}{H(L)}=4$$

The proposed multiplier is $5$, and therefore

$$4\ne5$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Keep the positive-domain restriction in view and isolate the power first:

$$40L^{\frac{2}{3}}=360$$

Divide by the coefficient:

$$L^{\frac{2}{3}}=9$$

Raise both sides to the reciprocal exponent:

$$L=(9)^{\frac{3}{2}}$$

$$L=27$$

Only the positive solution is admissible in this model. Comparing it with the proposed value gives

$$27=27.$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Composition is ordered: evaluate the inner map before the outer map.

$$g(6)=4(6)^2$$

$$g(6)=144$$

Insert that inner output into $f$:

$$f(g(6))=3\sqrt{144}$$

Complete the power evaluation:

$$3\cdot12$$

$$f(g(6))=36$$

The displayed claim is $24$, so

$$36\ne24$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim.

So the statement is False.
math.solution_overview:
Topics: growth_elastic, evaluate, scaling, solve, compose_inverse.
A: analyze percentage growth, elasticity, domain, or joint input scaling.
B: evaluate the C model at m=9.
C: derive the scale multiplier for H.
D: solve the positive power equation for L.
E: evaluate the two maps in their stated order.

Levels keep the scale factor $A$. Scale comparisons cancel $A$ and leave only the power of the input ratio. Recover $A$ and any unknown exponent once here; each letter only checks its extra claim.

math.title: Cubic deviation — critical points and values
math.context:
A production deviation is modelled by

$$
f(x)=x^{3}-6x^{2}+9x+1\qquad(x\in\mathbb{R})
$$

Decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: The derivative factors as $f'(x)=3(x-1)(x-3)$.
There is a local maximum at $x=1$.
The local-minimum value of $f$ is strictly less than $0$.
Between the two critical points, $f$ is strictly decreasing.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
f'(x)=3x^{2}-12x+9=3(x^{2}-4x+3)=3(x-1)(x-3)
$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$
f''(x)=6x-12,\qquad f''(1)=-6<0
$$

so $x=1$ is a local maximum.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

At the local minimum $x=3$:

$$
f(3)=27-54+27+1=1\nless 0
$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

On $(1,3)$ one has $f'(x)=3(x-1)(x-3)<0$, so $f$ is strictly decreasing between the critical points.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
f(0)=1,\qquad f(4)=64-96+36+1=5
$$

$$
f(0)+f(4)=6\neq 2
$$

So the statement is False.
math.solution_overview: $f'=3(x-1)(x-3)$; local max at $1$ ($f=5$), local min at $3$ ($f=1$). Decreasing on $(1,3)$. $f(0)+f(4)=6$.

math.title: Exponential biomass — doubling and window factors
math.context:
A culture’s biomass (in grams) follows

$$
B(t)=80\,e^{0.2t}\qquad(t\ge 0\text{ in hours})
$$

Decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: Initial biomass is exactly $80$ g.
Biomass doubles in strictly less than $4$ hours.
After $5$ hours, biomass already exceeds $200$ g.
The relative growth factor over any $5$-hour window is exactly $e$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
B(0)=80\,e^{0}=80
$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Doubling means $80e^{0.2t}=160$, so $e^{0.2t}=2$, hence

$$
t=\dfrac{\ln 2}{0.2}=5\ln 2\approx 5\cdot 0.693=3.465<4
$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$
B(5)=80e^{1}=80e\approx 80\cdot 2.718=217.4>200
$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

For any $t$,

$$
\dfrac{B(t+5)}{B(t)}=e^{0.2\cdot 5}=e
$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$
\dfrac{B(10)}{B(5)}=\dfrac{80e^{2}}{80e}=e
$$

So the statement is True.

math.title: Revenue and cost — marginals and a level check
math.context:
Weekly revenue and cost (in thousands of euros) for output $q>0$ are

$$
R(q)=30q-q^{2},\qquad C(q)=q^{3}-6q^{2}+15q+8
$$

Decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: Marginal revenue is $R'(q)=30-2q$.
Marginal cost is $C'(q)=3q^{2}-12q+15$.
At $q=3$, marginal revenue strictly exceeds marginal cost.
Profit $\pi=R-C$ has a critical point wherever $R'=C'$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Differentiate $R(q)=30q-q^{2}$:

$$
R'(q)=30-2q
$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$
C'(q)=3q^{2}-12q+15
$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

$$
\pi'(q)=R'(q)-C'(q)
$$

vanishes precisely when $R'=C'$.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
R(4)=120-16=104,\qquad C(4)=64-96+60+8=36
$$

$$
104\neq 36
$$

So the statement is False.

math.title: Two draws without replacement — colour events
math.context:
An urn holds $5$ red, $4$ blue and $3$ green balls ($12$ balls total). Two balls are drawn **without replacement**, order irrelevant.

Decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: The number of equally likely two-ball hands is $\binom{12}{2}=66$.
The probability both balls are red is strictly less than $\tfrac{1}{5}$.
The probability of one red and one blue equals $\dfrac{20}{66}$.
The probability both balls share a colour exceeds $\tfrac{1}{3}$.
The probability of at least one green ball equals $\dfrac{30}{66}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\binom{12}{2} = \dfrac{12 \cdot 11}{1 \cdot 2} = 66
$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$
P(\text{both red})=\dfrac{\binom{5}{2}}{66}=\dfrac{10}{66}=\dfrac{5}{33}\approx 0.152<\dfrac{1}{5}
$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Count mixed red-blue pairs: $5\cdot 4=20$ (unordered pairs, one of each colour).

$$
P=\dfrac{20}{66}
$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
P(\text{same colour})=\dfrac{\binom{5}{2}+\binom{4}{2}+\binom{3}{2}}{66}=\dfrac{10+6+3}{66}=\dfrac{19}{66}
$$

$$
\dfrac{19}{66}\approx 0.288\ngtr \dfrac{1}{3}
$$

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Complement: no green means both from the $9$ non-green balls.

$$
P(\text{at least one green})=1-\dfrac{\binom{9}{2}}{66}=1-\dfrac{36}{66}=\dfrac{30}{66}
$$

So the statement is True.
math.solution_overview: Universe $\binom{12}{2}=66$. Both red $10/66$. Red-blue $20/66$. Same colour $19/66$. At least one green $30/66$.

math.title: Binomial defectives — mean, variance, and a PMF term
math.context:
A machine produces items independently with defect probability $p=0.2$. A batch of $n=10$ items is inspected. Let $X$ be the number of defectives, so $X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(10,0.2)$.

Decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: The mean number of defectives is exactly $2$.
The variance is strictly less than $2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
E[X]=np=10\cdot 0.2=2
$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$
\mathrm{Var}(X)=np(1-p)=10\cdot 0.2\cdot 0.8=1.6<2
$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

The binomial PMF at $k=2$ is exactly that product form, and

$$
\binom{10}{2} = \dfrac{10 \cdot 9}{1 \cdot 2} = 45
$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$
P(X\ge 1)=1-P(X=0)\approx 1-0.1074=0.8926>0.85
$$

So the statement is True.
